header: Inputs and a formula, but no total
lead: One row per cost item, with its rate and a line on how to count it. The formula sits below, in rich text.
bodytext:
Total = base + (quantity × rate) + extras

Editors write the formula in the rich text and can add a worked example. The element does no maths itself, because a calculated figure would be a quote nobody at the company has checked.
note: The note says which rates apply and what overrides them, usually a written offer.

inputs.title: The cost item is the row header
inputs.text: So screen readers announce what each rate applies to.

inputs.title: The rate keeps its own column
inputs.text: Rates sit flush right in their own column, so the amounts line up.

inputs.title: How to count it is the third column
inputs.text: Where to find the number to multiply: last month's invoice, a statistics page or a headcount.

inputs.title: A rate can be a range
inputs.text: Not everything has a single price.
